title: Fleet utilization signal analysis — daily anomaly digest
body:
Purpose:
This is a working export + short analysis of the GPU fleet daily utilization signals across clusters and pools for 2025-07-10 -> 2025-07-14. Focus: surface operational anomalies (unexpected drops/spikes), region-specific saturation trends, and immediate mitigations. Not a final runbook — notes + action items below.

Executive summary:
- Overall fleet average utilization (vGPU-equivalent) for 2025-07-10..14: 58% (weighted by capacity).
- Two notable anomalies detected:
  1) 2025-07-13 03:00 UTC — us-central-1: inference-prod pool experienced a 16% utilization drop sustained for 4 hours while request rates were stable (likely preemption or node retirement).
  2) 2025-07-14 11:00 UTC — eu-west-1: burst in batch-training pool utilization to 94% concurrent with OOM errors on a subset of P4d hosts (suspected image/driver mismatch after kernel update).
- Trending concern: APAC region (ap-northeast-1 + ap-southeast-1) shows gradual growth in 90th-percentile latency correlated with thermal throttling alerts on older A100 hosts (fleet age 22-28 months).

Notes on metrics and how they were computed:
- avg-util% = average of per-GPU utilization samples recorded at 1-min resolution, weighted by GPU count per node.
- p95-util% computed from per-minute per-cluster distribution.
- peak-minute-util% represents the single minute maximum observed in the day.
- active-nodes = nodes reporting health and joined to Kubernetes pool at midnight UTC.
- Anomalies flagged by our rule engine when utilization deviates by >12% from a rolling 7-day baseline AND cluster-level request-rate does not drop by >8%.

Anomaly deep-dive #1 — us-central-1 sustained drop (2025-07-13 03:00-07:00 UTC):
Observed behavior:
- inference-prod pool utilization dropped from baseline 66% -> 50% at 03:00 UTC and recovered by 07:10 UTC.
- Request rates (RPS) for inference-prod remained within +/-3% of baseline (no traffic change).
- Node autoscaler logs show 4 node terminations in that window; cloud provider lists preemptions on 4 instances with reasons: host-maintenance (2), soft-preempt (2).
- No corresponding increase in tail latency reported by app-level tracing; downstream retries are low.
Preliminary hypothesis:
- Capacity loss driven by host-level preemptions; autoscaler reacted but replacement nodes came up with lower initial scheduling density (taints/tolerations) causing temporary capacity gap.
Immediate mitigations taken:
- Manual scaling +2 nodes initiated at 03:12 UTC (elastic-reserve).
- Scheduling tolerations adjusted in inference-prod DaemonSet to accept replacement nodes while they join.
Open questions / next steps:
- Verify provider maintenance window settings and request guaranteed host protection for critical pools (JIRA-ENG-4821 assigned).
- Add pro-active simulation test for 3% capacity loss to ensure autoscaler warmup meets SLO.

Anomaly deep-dive #2 — eu-west-1 OOM spike (2025-07-14 11:00 UTC):
Observed behavior:
- batch-training pool hit sustained p95 utilization 94% and emitted node-level OOMs on 5/15 P4d hosts; job retries increased 3x.
- Kernel/driver rollout noted in rollout logs: gpu-driver v525.60 -> v525.80 staged 2025-07-14 08:30 UTC in eu-west-1 (canary-first).
Hypothesis:
- New driver exposed slightly different memory characteristics leading to higher reserved memory footprint for container runtime; combined with the batch-training job sizing (mem-constrained) resulted in OOMs.
Mitigations and findings:
- Rolled back driver on affected hosts at 12:10 UTC; incident reduced but two jobs already retried.
- Recorded diagnostic traces and kernel logs attached to JIRA-ENG-4833.
Action items:
- Pin driver version for batch-training pool until expanded canary validated (owner: Priya Srinivasan).
- Run synthetic memory-pressure test across host images before driver rollout (owner: Leo Martinez).

Regional trend: APAC thermal/latency growth
- Observed correlation between increased 90th latency and thermal throttling events on A100-40GB older hosts in ap-northeast-1 and ap-southeast-1.
- Fleet age for these hosts: 22-28 months; BIOS firmware version lag noted.
- Suggested triage: schedule a firmware update and redistribute hot workloads to newer host classes (A100-80GB, H100 mixed) to lower thermal density.

Capacity planning notes and short-term recommendations:
1) Warm reserve for inference-prod in critical regions: keep 6% of regional capacity as pre-provisioned nodes (elastic-reserve) to cover short preemption events (simulation required).
2) Driver rollout policy: extend canary from 2 nodes -> 10 nodes and include batch-training job footprint tests (5-run min).
3) Fleet refresh prioritization: mark A100-40GB hosts >20 months for replacement or rebalancing into cooler failure domains.
4) Autoscaler tuning: shorten join/scheduling warmup window by adjusting pod disruption budgets and kube-scheduler toleration timeouts.

Open TODOs (short):
- [ ] Run 3%-loss autoscaler warmup simulation for us-central-1 (owner: Aaron Patel) — due 2025-07-20.
- [ ] Implement driver preflight memory profiler in rollout pipeline (owner: Priya) — due 2025-07-24.
- [ ] Plan APAC firmware updates and hot-workload migration play (owner: Maya) — due 2025-07-30.
- [ ] Add anomaly-runbook snippet to confluence: infra/gpu-anomalies (owner: Leo) — due 2025-07-18.

Notes-to-self / working thoughts (fragmented):
- Could consider using node labeling strategy to prefer lower-util hosts for batch-training rather than hard isolate; helps smooth thermal hotspots.
- Need clearer metric for GPU memory pressure (currently approximate via OOM events + mem-allocated samples). A per-container GPU-mem sampler would help.
- Investigate whether cloud provider preemption metadata can be surfaced earlier (push to provider support).
